title: Unify GPU memory pools and introduce a slot reclaimer operator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last two years the serving runtime accumulated multiple specialized GPU memory pools (io-buffer-pool, kv-warmup-pool, slot-local-alloc, prefetch-buffer) each with bespoke lifecycle code. This fragmentation causes uneven memory utilization under bursty workloads, increases GC-like eviction edge cases, and complicates scheduler heuristics. Goal: Consolidate heterogeneous pools into a unified memory pool abstraction with a programmable slot reclaimer operator that can reclaim underutilized slot allocations based on multi-dimensional signals (age, kv-access-activity, inferred session stickiness). Scope: refactor pool implementations into PoolManager, add Reclaimer operator, expose operational knobs via the existing scheduler config, add metrics/traces and e2e tests, and perform a canary rollout on a non-critical cluster. Out of scope: application-level allocator rewrite, driver/kernel changes, and persistent KV store semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Single unified GPU pool replaces previous io-buffer-pool and slot-local-alloc implementations behind a feature flag
Slot reclaimer operator reclaims >90% of idle slot allocations within configured TTL without increasing tail latency beyond 5% under synthetic burst tests
No regression in end-to-end median and p95 token latency on the staging performance dashboard compared to the baseline run
New metrics available: pool_total_bytes, pool_used_bytes, reclaimed_slots_count, reclaim_latency_ms, reclaim_reason_label
Automated integration tests covering race between reclaim and batch commit added to CI
Canary rollout plan documented and executed with automatic rollback on SLO breaches
technical_notes: Design: introduce PoolManager (thin facade) that manages slabs and free lists; keep a lightweight per-tenant partition map to avoid hotkey contention. SlotReclaimer observes session activity via recent KV touch events and scheduler admission signals. Reclaimer runs in an operator thread pool and uses cooperative backoff to avoid contention with the IO thread. Eviction policy: prefer slots with zero KV reads in last N seconds, then oldest by last-touch, and finally lowest inferred priority from admission token. Compatibility: expose feature flag runtime.unified_pool.enabled; when disabled, fall back to current pools. Rollout strategy: enable unified pool read-only mode (allocation served but reclamation disabled) to validate accounting, then enable reclamation on canary nodes. Safety: reclamation never steals slots with active commit-phase flag; commit-phase annotated on slot descriptors. Observability: add tracing spans for pool.allocate, pool.free, reclaimer.run; sample 1% of traces for high-frequency paths. Performance regression risk: new allocator must avoid lock contention—use sharded free lists per NUMA/GPU-stream. Memory accounting note: small transient overshoot allowed up to 8% to avoid forced synchronous reclaim under spikes.

Implement SlotReclaimer operator and policy engine (Mateo)
Add metrics/tracing and dashboard tiles (Observability team)
